recipes.name: Philadelphia Classic Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups HONEY MAID Graham Cracker Crumbs
4 (8 ounce) packages PHILADELPHIA Cream Cheese, softened

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Mix cookie crumbs, butter, and 3 tablespoons sugar together until combined; press firmly onto the bottom of a 9-inch nonstick springform pan.
Beat cream cheese, 1 cup sugar, and vanilla in a mixing bowl until smooth.
Add eggs, one at a time, mixing on low speed until just blended. Pour over crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until center is almost set, about 45 to 55 minutes.
Loosen cake from the pan rim; cool before removing rim.

raw_recipe.headline: Philadelphia Classic Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This Philadelphia cheesecake recipe makes a simple, classic cheesecake that’s smooth and creamy with no water bath needed. Sure to be a hit!

review.reviewBody: this was an easy and great tasting cheesecake. My family loved it and it was easy to make

Everyone who has eaten my Philadelphia Cheesecake recipe says it's the creamiest, tastiest and best cheesecake they have ever eaten. I always add 1/4 c heavy whipping cream, just for a creamier texture and I always put 1 tablespoon of Watkins Real Vanilla Extract. We like more vanilla flavor and Watkins is the best I've found. My Grannie always used it when the Watkin's man use to home deliver. Tip: I also put a medium size stainless steel bowl of water in the oven while it preheats and leaving it in during the bake keeps it from getting dry. I found this works better for me than when I tried baking the dish in a water bath. I also wrap foil around the sides of the dish and loosely lay foil on top removing the top foil the last 5 minutes fo baking, as we don't like a brown top cheesecake. I use the white, oval shaped Pyrex dish, as it does make a large cake and I bake mine on 350 for 45 min's. It's still jiggly like Jello and sets perfect when cools. I had to bake a few trial and error times before getting the tweaks to our liking. Once I got it down it is the Easiest Cheesecake I have every made!

Really great base recipe. I ended up adding about 3/4 cup (ish) of heavy cream to give it a little more velvety texture. Definitely used a water bath after wrapping the springform pan in aluminum foil too. And then when it was done cooking I cooled it slowly, first in the oven with the heat off and the door cracked, and then later on just on the counter. No cracks, and smooth as silk. Top this sucker with a little chocolate ganache and some sliced strawberries and it'll get gobbled up like it's got the antidote.

I've been making this for at least 40 years. I don't think I've ever had one fail. I save about a cup of the batter, add about 3 tablespoons of cocoa mix well, then drop by spoonfuls on top of the batter already in the pan Take a table knife and gently swirl. It's pretty enough to skip the topping, but cherry pie filling takes it to another level.
Made two. When chilled added sour cream on top of one with shortbread cookie crust, let set then put cherry pie filling on top and the other with filling on top without sour cream.

I have been eating this since I was a little girl. My mother made it. My favorite dessert except for sweet potatoe pie. My great grandmothers recipe. Take 1/2 cp Sr cream mix with 1/2 cp sugar pour on top bake 15 to 20 min more. You can mix this and add the last 20 of cooking time. Delicious.

My favorite cheesecake recipe. It's so easy and incredibly easy to add different flavors. I use Oreos for the crust. I use a whole pack and a stick of butter and make 2 thinner cheesecakes with the same amount of cheesecake mix. A single is too thick and rich for us. 2 is perfect!

I made this for a birthday. I made another birthday cake so I halved the recipe and baked in a pie plate. I added some heavy cream as other users suggested and baked in the water bath. The other change I made was to make the crust using smashed oreo cookies and folded a few smashed oreo bits into the mixture. The cheese cake was a hit and looked beautiful. I can see this recipe working with other add in ingredients. I may try pecans next.

I added more sugar and a cup of heavy cream to the recipe. Baked it a bit longer. It was the ABSOLUTE BEST cheesecake I've ever had in my entire life. Others said they had expected that I bought it from the cheesecake factory.
Whole family loved it! I made an oreo crust and chopped up oreos in the batter. Topped it with stabilized whipped cream and oreo halves. It was a huge success and a new family favorite!
I added caramel Hersey syrup and pecans chips to make a turtle cheesecake
My mother would make this every 4th of July. Decide to try my hand. She always topped with blueberries and cherries.

I make this cheesecake for all the birthdays in my family, my wedding anniversary, and holidays. It is easy to adapt the flavors in this recipe. My suggestion is never use a substitute for Philadelphia Cream Cheeze and don’t use low fat either. If you do either of those things, you will not like the taste.

I have made several variations of this cheesecake. I used coconut extract and coconut flakes in the mix, and I topped it with toasted coconut. Also, I have used strawberry extract and pureed strawberries to swirl into the mix,then topped with fresh strawberries. Very versatile recipe. 5 Stars.
I loved it! Plus it was fun to make.
Ez to make
Very easy recipe to follow for perfect results. Only change I make is an oreo crust and crushed oreos mixed in batter. Absolutely delicious!
Used an old kraft version of this recipe that my mother-in-law had that had to add 1 cup of sour cream. I also like a more vanilla flavor, so used 3 TBSP of Costco's pure vanilla extract.
Added Almond Flavoring in place of Vanilla. Delicious

I’ve used this recipe for years, to the point that I got a little careless with the directions. I set the oven at 350 rather than 325, and didn’t notice until about 35 minutes into the bake. I immediately decreased the heat, then removed the cake after a total of 45 minutes. After 30 minutes of cooling, it didn’t look set, and the knife test confirmed that. Back into a 325 oven for 10 minutes - then the top was quite brown to the point I was ready to make another one. Inspired by a recent taste of a Basque cheesecake, I took this one to our gathering. It was a hit, and even I thought it tasted great!
